header: Date: 2026-01-08 10:00 PT | Duration: 64 mins | Location: Zoom | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Monroe (PineHarbor Platform Eng), Dr. Sofia Chen (PineHarbor Security), Luis Ortega (PineHarbor SRE)
summary: Technical readiness / certification discussion for PineHarbor's marketplace connector listing and private deployment playbook. Focus on Helm packaging, KMS integration, init containers for node prep, image signing, FIPS compliance, and a plan for staged certification and a 2-hour baseline perf run.
transcript:
00:00:00 Jordan Lee: Okay, hi everyone, thanks for joining, we've got about an hour, um, run through cert steps and deployment playbook.
00:00:14 Alex Monroe: Thanks Jordan. Quick note — Sofia's on for the security bits, Luis is here for SRE. We're mainly worried about packaging and how Redwood's connector behaves in our GovCloud... 
00:00:27 Dr. Sofia Chen: Yep, and we need to confirm KMS paths, audit logs, and whether the images are FIPS/CIS hardened. Also attestation for supply chain is important.
00:00:40 Maya Patel: Totally. We'll start with the Helm chart and the service mesh sidecar pattern we recommend, then KMS config and certs, then the conformance checklist.
00:00:55 Luis Ortega: One thing we hit last time with another vendor — the init container required sysctl changes and we couldn't run on our managed nodes without nodeAffinity exceptions. Any workarounds?
00:01:08 Maya Patel: Yeah, we have a lightweight init that runs as non-privileged and uses a hostPath minimal shim; but for GovCloud we can switch to a DaemonSet-based nodeprep job. It's in the repo, see link in chat (redwood.co/pineharbor-helm).
00:01:26 Alex Monroe: I saw that link, thanks. Is that shim signed? We need image signing and SLSA attestation for the pipeline.
00:01:34 Jordan Lee: We sign images with cosign in our CI; we can provide signed manifests and provenance. Maya, can you call out the artifact docs?
00:01:42 Maya Patel: Yes — we publish cosign signatures and we can add a verification step in the Helm pre-install hook; we'll attach the example script.
00:01:54 Dr. Sofia Chen: Good. On KMS, we run AWS KMS with separate CMKs per environment, and we require envelope encryption plus audit trails forwarded to our Splunk index. How does Redwood key wrapping integrate?
00:02:08 Maya Patel: Support for external KMS is built into the connector: you can supply a KMS alias in values.yaml, and the runtime will call a KMS client using IAM role. For audit forwarding, we emit structured audit events to stdout which you can capture with a sidecar or FluentD. There are a couple of small caveats with STS tokens refresh; we'll note those in the playbook.
00:02:31 Luis Ortega: That sounds ok. Do you support HSM-backed KMS like CloudHSM? We need FIPS mode for one of our workloads.
00:02:39 Maya Patel: We can support HSM-backed keys if the KMS endpoint provides a compatible envelope API. For FIPS we also have a FIPS image variant — it's larger but prebuilt. We need to run a simple regression test for crypto calls.
00:02:55 Alex Monroe: Great. Moving to packaging — marketplace listing wants a single-tenant connector bundle that can be installed via marketplace UI, plus a private helm repo. How do we produce an OLM/Helm bundle that passes their validator?
00:03:10 Jordan Lee: Our recommended pattern is: Helm chart + OCI image signed + an operator-like wrapper that exposes readiness probes and healthchecks. For the marketplace validator, we already keep a policy file. Maya, do we have a preflight checklist for the marketplace validators?
00:03:25 Maya Patel: We do. It includes manifest linting, CVE scanning artifacts, an SBOM, cosign proofs, and a health probe conformance test. I'll drop the checklist link in Slack after this call.
00:03:36 Dr. Sofia Chen: Are SBOMs generated automatically in the pipeline? We need SPDX preferred.
00:03:42 Maya Patel: We output SPDX-compliant SBOMs by default from the build pipeline. The build artifact in the repo shows an example sbom.spdx.json.
00:03:50 Luis Ortega: On networking — the connector opens a control plane port and an outbound to Redwood's ingestion endpoints; for airgapped installs we need a pull-only model. Is that supported?
00:04:03 Maya Patel: We support pull-only with an offline bundle: image tarballs plus a configuration file that points to an internal ingestion gateway. For completely air-gapped installs we have an onprem agent package.
00:04:15 Alex Monroe: Perfect. About performance — we need a 95th percentile latency target for short-chat workloads under 200ms; can we run a perf baseline in our VPC?
00:04:27 Jordan Lee: Yes, we propose a 2-hour baseline with scripted traffic generator. It will exercise batching and KV cache warmup. It helps us determine quantization and batching knobs for your workload.
00:04:40 Luis Ortega: OK — we'll provision the test VPC and provide an IAM role with restricted rights.
00:04:47 Maya Patel: For the perf harness we need a sample prompt set; if you can share 200-300 representative prompts that's ideal.
00:04:56 Alex Monroe: We'll produce a seed set and scrub PII. Any SSO/SAML questions for enterprise onboarding?
00:05:05 Dr. Sofia Chen: SSO is needed for console access, and we need RBAC mapping to our LDAP groups.
00:05:12 Jordan Lee: The console supports SAML 2.0 and SCIM for group sync. We'll send a mapping guide.
00:05:19 Maya Patel: Side note: for the private install we recommend enabling token-level encryption at rest, and rotate keys every 90 days — playbook includes a step-by-step KMS rotation snippet.
00:05:33 Alex Monroe: Excellent. One more security ops question — audit logs retention: we retain 2 years, but for marketplace listing they ask for 90 days. Is that configurable?
00:05:45 Maya Patel: Yes, retention is configurable per-install; export to long-term storage is also supported. We'll note recommended retention default in the document.
00:05:56 Jordan Lee: Cool. Any blockers on compliance stage for PineHarbor?
00:06:01 Dr. Sofia Chen: Sidestepping the pipeline attestation and verifying the SBOMs are the two items. Also want to validate the preflight checks in a sandbox prior to listing.
00:06:12 Jordan Lee: Plan: Redwood sends hardened helm + prod values and the preflight checklist by Monday. PineHarbor provisions VPC and we schedule the perf run week of Jan 19. We'll loop in security to validate SBOM & cosign. Sound OK?
00:06:25 Alex Monroe: Yes, sounds good.
00:06:28 Luis Ortega: Quick note — for our CI we use GitLab; the cosign step needs to be a job we can copy. Can you give a minimal GitLab CI snippet?
00:06:36 Maya Patel: Yes, I'll paste an example in the playbook, minimal 3 steps: build, cosign, push. I'll also include a preflight verify job.
00:06:47 Jordan Lee: Great. Anything else? If not we'll wrap and circulate notes and next steps.
00:06:52 Dr. Sofia Chen: No, just make sure the FIPS image and SBOM are attached.
00:06:57 Jordan Lee: Noted. Thanks everyone.
00:06:59 Alex Monroe: Thanks.
00:07:02 [call ends]

Notes: Transcript has normal ASR errors, some product names may be transcribed differently (e.g., 'cosign' sometimes 'co-sign'), timestamps approximate. Links referenced in chat: https://redwood.co/pineharbor-helm, https://redwood.co/pineharbor-playbook
